services.name: Telegram
setup_steps: Open Telegram on your phone or desktop
Search for @BotFather
Send /newbot
Choose a display name (e.g. "My Foreman Bot")
Choose a username ending in 'bot' (e.g. acme_foreman_bot)
Copy the token BotFather sends

extra_secrets.name: telegram-chat-id
extra_secrets.description: Where the bot should send messages (your DM or a group chat).
setup_steps: Open your bot in Telegram, press Start and send it any message
Easiest: press Enter here to skip. Foreman finds your chat for you: on the Services page press [n], or run foreman notify enable telegram
Or open https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates and paste the chat.id you see

services.name: Discord
setup_steps: Open discord.com/developers/applications → New Application, and name it
Bot tab → Reset Token → Copy (no privileged intents are needed)
OAuth2 → URL Generator: scopes bot and applications.commands, permissions Send Messages and Embed Links
Open the generated URL and add the bot to your server

services.name: Slack
setup_steps: Visit api.slack.com/apps → 'Create New App'
Choose 'From scratch', name the app, pick your workspace
OAuth & Permissions → Bot Token Scopes — add at minimum:
[x] chat:write     → post messages as the bot
[x] channels:read  → list public channels the bot can reach
Optional bot scopes — only add if your agent actually needs them:
[ ] im:history     → read DM history with the bot
[ ] files:write    → upload files / images
[ ] groups:read    → list private channels the bot is in
Install to Workspace (top of the OAuth page) → Authorize
Copy the 'Bot User OAuth Token' (starts with xoxb-)
In the channel for alerts, type /invite @your-bot

services.name: GitHub
services.description: Personal Access Token for repo access
setup_steps: Visit github.com/settings/tokens/new
Name: 'Foreman agent token' (or anything memorable)
Expiration: 90 days recommended
Required scopes — tick these two:
[x] repo       → read + write to your repos (public + private)
[x] read:user  → read your profile (display name, email)
Optional scopes — only tick if your agent actually needs them:
[ ] read:org   → list your org memberships
[ ] workflow   → trigger GitHub Actions
[ ] gist       → read + write your gists
Click 'Generate token' at the bottom
Copy immediately (won't show again — starts with ghp_)

services.name: Atlassian (Jira / Confluence)
setup_steps: Visit id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens
Create API token → name it
Copy the token

services.name: Notion
setup_steps: Visit notion.so/my-integrations
New integration → name it
Choose workspace + capabilities
Copy the Internal Integration Token
Share each Notion page you want the integration to access
